text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday's morning German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl firmly rejects criticism in CDU/CSU coalition of Finance Minister Theo Waigel after calls for Waigel's resignation
- At reform communist PDS party congress Lothar Bisky confirmed in office as party leader for two more years
- The opposition Social Democrats demand a supplementary budget for 1997
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem says that pension levels can not be sustained and renews call for lowering pensions
HANDELSBLATT
- Car company shares are dollar winners. The mark will remain weak against the dollar and some European currencies in 1997, according to bank analysts
- The supervisory board of troubled engineering group Deutsche Babcock will decide whether Heyo Schmiedeknecht should remain on its board chairman
- Bonn Justice Ministry wages battle against money laundering
- Oppposition Social Democrats want a supplementary budget because of gap in budget
- Kohl supports Finance Minister Theo Waigel, after calls from within the CDU/CSU for his resignation
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, who met Serbian opposition leader Zoran Djindjic on Sunday, says sanctions against Serbia would not be appropriate at present
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Opposition Social Democrats' drugs bill, which proposes authorities should not criminalise drug addicts, is heavily criticised by Kohl's Christian Democrats
- Bonn tax debate prompts calls for Finance Minister Theo Waigel's resignation
- HDE retailers' federation calls for tougher measures against shoplifters
- German car production rose in 1996 by four percent
DIE WELT
- Kohl defends record of Finance Minister Theo Waigel and rejects calls in CDU for his resignation
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem expects lower pension levels
- Annual party congress of reform communist party of Democratic Socialism (PDS) ends with a defeat for its leadership, after delegates rejected toning down party's Communist platform
- Heyo Schmiedknecht, chairman of the supervisory board at troubled engineering group Deutsche Babcock AG, will have to step down. Board meet today to decide his fate
- Possible case of BSE or "madcow disease" in Hoexter district in western Germany

- Row over the budget: opposition Social Democrats (SPD) threaten they will take case to the supreme court. SPD demands that Finance Minister Theo Waigel present a supplementary budget when he unveils main budget for 1997 on January 28
- German regional states want to cap coal subsidies. Liberal Free Democrats support proposal Bonn subsidies should be reduced to two billion marks from 10 billion marks a year
